titulo: Unreal Past, Modal Perfect and Third Conditional
descripcion: At B2 the three regret structures — wish, modal perfect, third conditional — are learned individually and start to be combined in short exchanges. The seamless blending expected at C1 isn't the target yet; using each correctly, and occasionally together, is enough.

filas: regret about now or the past
if + past perfect, would have + participle

ejemplos.texto: I wish I'd known about it sooner.
We should have checked before leaving.
If we'd checked, we wouldn't have missed the train.

notas: Wish takes the past perfect when the regret is about the past: I wish I'd known, not I wish I knew, for a past event.
Should have is about a missed obligation; could have is about a missed possibility — they aren't interchangeable.
The if-clause of the third conditional never contains would.

contraste.es: Spanish expresses the same with ojalá + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo and with si + pluscuamperfecto + conditional perfect, and it also has the modal perfect (debería haberlo dicho, podría haberlo evitado). The logic is parallel; the difference is the form, since Spanish puts the modal in the conditional and English uses should / could have + participle.
contraste.de: German has close equivalents for all three pieces: ich wünschte, ich hätte… (I wish I had), hätte… sollen / können (should / could have) and hätte… in conditionals. The recurring error comes from colloquial würde: I wish I would have known, if I would have known.
contraste.it: Italian has a separate modal perfect (avrei dovuto, avrei potuto), so all three pieces exist. Translated literally, however, avrei dovuto dirtelo becomes I would have had to tell you instead of I should have told you.
contraste.fr: French has a separate modal perfect (j'aurais dû, j'aurais pu) and si seulement j'avais su for regret, so all three pieces exist. Translated literally, j'aurais dû te le dire becomes I would have had to tell you instead of I should have told you.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has the modal perfect in almost the same order as English (devia ter dito – should have said; podia ter evitado – could have avoided). Together with quem me dera ter sabido (I wish I had known), all three pieces transfer well.

errores: Using would in the if-clause of the third conditional.
Confusing should have and could have.
Using the past simple after wish for a past regret instead of the past perfect.

es: *tendría que haber ido* rendered as *I would have to have gone* instead of *I should have gone*.
de: *wenn … nur* rendered with *when*: *When I had only known* instead of *If only I had known*.
it: *sarei dovuto venire* rendered as *I would have had to come*, which changes the meaning, instead of *I should have come*.
fr: *j'aurais dû venir* rendered as *I would have had to come*, which changes the meaning, instead of *I should have come*.
pt: *devia ter vindo* rendered as *I had to come*, which states a fact, instead of *I should have come*.

traducciones.de: sich für etwas begeistern / in etwas einsteigen
Wenn wir… hätten, hätten wir nicht…
traducciones.fr: Si nous avions…, nous n’aurions pas…

redemittel.funcion: regret about something that was done

redemittel.expresion: There was nothing we could have done.

traducciones.es: No había nada que pudiéramos haber hecho.
traducciones.pt: Não havia nada que pudéssemos ter feito.

redemittel.funcion: turns the regret into a plan

traducciones.fr: En fait, je ne le regrette pas.
traducciones.it: In realtà non me ne pento.

redemittel.funcion: hands the counterfactual to the other person

traducciones.pt: E tu, o que terias feito?

mision.consigna: Write about a hobby you gave up and what you'd do differently.
requisitos: use *to take up a hobby*, *club* and *leisure activity*

microtareas.texto: Write three *I wish I'd…* sentences about a *club* you left.
Turn one into *If I'd…, I would have…*.
Record 90 seconds: what *should* you *have* done to *relax* more last year?

autochequeo: Is the past perfect used after wish for a past regret?
Are should have and could have used correctly, not interchangeably?
Is the if-clause free of would?
Are at least two of the three structures used in the same passage?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on wish, modal perfect and the third conditional. Check for would inside the if-clause and the choice between should and could have. Do not rewrite the text.
